fields.summary: Bug 2488714 - freeipa server fails on Fedora 44

status.description: Initial creation status. Implies nothing yet and should be very short lived; also can be a Bugzilla status.
status.name: New

items.fromString:
*Summary:*

The caOCSPCert certificate profile is missing the SubjectKeyIdentifier (SKI) extension, causing external CA installation to fail during step 2 when creating the OCSP signing certificate.

#  The bootstrap profile (base/ca/shared/conf/caOCSPCert.profile) defines the SubjectKeyIdentifier extension as item 7 (lines 16-18), but item 7 is NOT included in the active list on line 9: list=2,4,8,9,10. This means the extension definition is present but never activated.

This has been the case since commit [https://github.com/dogtagpki/pki/commit/dc03fc45781bbabf20aec8505868ed51aad2b2e6|https://github.com/dogtagpki/pki/commit/dc03fc45781bbabf20aec8505868ed51aad2b2e6|smart-link]  (2017) which reworked the profile to remove KeyUsage (item 6) and add OCSPNoCheck (item 10), but did not add item 7 to the list. The old list was list=2,4,6,8,9 and the new list became list=2,4,8,9,10, skipping 7.

# The runtime profile (base/ca/shared/profiles/ca/caOCSPCert.cfg) also has no SubjectKeyIdentifier policy at all. The policy set list on line 13 is: policyset.ocspCertSet.list=1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 — no item 7, and no subjectKeyIdentifierExtDefaultImpl defined anywhere in the file.

By comparison, caCACert.cfg correctly includes subjectKeyIdentifierExtDefaultImpl (as item 8 in its policy set), as do other CA certificate profiles.

Without the SKI extension, OCSP signing certificates violate RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.2, which states that the SKI extension SHOULD be present on all certificates.

Additionally, the profiles caInternalAuthOCSPCert.cfg and caCMCocspCert.cfg are missing the SKI extension.

*Version-Release number of selected component (if applicable):*

{noformat}# rpm -qa | grep pki-server
redhat-pki-server-11.10.0-1.el10_2.noarch{noformat}



*How reproducible:*
Always

*Steps to Reproduce:*
1. Install DS instance
2. Install a CA using external CA method (pkispawn step 1 and step 2)
3. Observe OCSP signing cert creation during step 2

*Actual results:*
- pki-server ca-cert-create --profile caOCSPCert.profile fails during OCSP cert creation
- The generated OCSP signing certificate has no SubjectKeyIdentifier extension
- External CA installation tests fail (externalca_nssdb-topo-03)

*Expected results:*
- The caOCSPCert profile should include SubjectKeyIdentifier, matching other CA cert profiles
- OCSP signing certificates should contain the SKI extension per RFC 5280
- External CA step 2 installation should complete successfully

*Additional info:*
The fix is to add SubjectKeyIdentifier to both profile files:

# caOCSPCert.profile: change list=2,4,8,9,10 to list=2,4,7,8,9,10
# caOCSPCert.cfg: add item 7 to policyset.ocspCertSet.list and add the following policy definition:
policyset.ocspCertSet.7.constraint.class_id=noConstraintImpl
policyset.ocspCertSet.7.constraint.name=No Constraint
policyset.ocspCertSet.7.default.class_id=subjectKeyIdentifierExtDefaultImpl
policyset.ocspCertSet.7.default.name=Subject Key Identifier Extension Default
policyset.ocspCertSet.7.default.params.critical=false

3. Observe OCSP signing cert creation during step 2

*Actual results:*

- The generated OCSP signing certificate has no SubjectKeyIdentifier extension
- External CA installation tests fail (externalca_nssdb-topo-03)

- External CA step 2 installation should complete successfully

# caOCSPCert.profile: change list=2,4,8,9,10 to list=2,4,7,8,9,10

policyset.ocspCertSet.7.constraint.class_id=noConstraintImpl
policyset.ocspCertSet.7.constraint.name=No Constraint
policyset.ocspCertSet.7.default.class_id=subjectKeyIdentifierExtDefaultImpl
policyset.ocspCertSet.7.default.name=Subject Key Identifier Extension Default
policyset.ocspCertSet.7.default.params.critical=false

items.fromString:
The caOCSPCert certificate profile is missing the SubjectKeyIdentifier (SKI) extension, causing external CA installation to fail during step 2 when creating the OCSP signing certificate.

# The bootstrap profile (base/ca/shared/conf/caOCSPCert.profile) defines the SubjectKeyIdentifier extension as item 7 (lines 16-18), but item 7 is NOT included in the active list on line 9: list=2,4,8,9,10. This means the extension definition is present but never activated.

This has been the case since commit dc03fc4578 (2017) by Endi Dewata, which reworked the profile to remove KeyUsage (item 6) and add OCSPNoCheck (item 10), but did not add item 7 to the list. The old list was list=2,4,6,8,9 and the new list became list=2,4,8,9,10, skipping 7.

# The runtime profile (base/ca/shared/profiles/ca/caOCSPCert.cfg) also has no SubjectKeyIdentifier policy at all. The policy set list on line 13 is: policyset.ocspCertSet.list=1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 — no item 7, and no subjectKeyIdentifierExtDefaultImpl defined anywhere in the file.

By comparison, caCACert.cfg correctly includes subjectKeyIdentifierExtDefaultImpl (as item 8 in its policy set), as do other CA certificate profiles.

Without the SKI extension, OCSP signing certificates violate RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.2, which states that the SKI extension SHOULD be present on all certificates.

`KRATool` command now supports a preliminary implementation of cross-scheme migration, allowing migration of archived keys between different key wrapping schemes (e.g., DES3 to AES, RSA to RSA-OAEP). This includes a standalone build mechanism for pki-kratool RPM.  This preliminary implementation currently contain a few unresolved issues:

- When the source and target payload wrap algorithm names are identical but the key sizes differ (e.g., AES-128 to AES-256 using "AES KeyWrap/Padding" for both),
  KRATool generates a session key with the source key size instead of the target key size. (DOGTAG-4496)
  - Cross-scheme migration from DES3 source keys fails because the session key unwrap is hardcoded to use AES. DES3 source keys require DES3 key type with 168-bit
  strength for the unwrap operation. (DOGTAG-4496)
  - When migrating to an HSM target (e.g., Luna), the target payload wrap algorithm must be set to "AES KeyWrap/Wrapped" instead of the default "AES KeyWrap/Padding". The default maps to an NSS-proprietary PKCS#11 mechanism that HSMs cannot process. (DOGTAG-4497)

The `KRATool` command now supports cross-scheme migration, allowing you to migrate archived keys between different key wrapping schemes, such as 3DES to AES and RSA to RSA-OAEP.
+

+

Two new tools for HSM compatibility verification:

    hsmCompatVerifyServ - Server-side simulator for CA and KRA operations

    hsmCompatVerifyClnt - Client-side simulator for certificate enrollment

These tools verify basic HSM compatibility with Dogtag Certificate System without requiring a full Certificate System installation, supporting RSA/ECC key operations, key archival/recovery workflows, and PKCS#12 export.
items.toString:
New tools added for HSM compatibility verification::
This update introduces two simulation tools to verify basic Hardware Security Module (HSM) compatibility with the Dogtag Certificate System without requiring a full installation:
+

* `hsmCompatVerifyServ` - A server-side simulator for Certificate Authority (CA) and Key Recovery Authority (KRA) operations.

* `hsmCompatVerifyClnt` - A client-side simulator for certificate enrollment.

Both tools support RSA and ECC key operations, key archival and recovery workflows, and PKCS#12 export. As a result, you can validate HSM integration and functionality before deploying a complete Certificate System environment.

A standalone command-line tool that allows HSM vendors and customers to verify
basic HSM compatibility with Dogtag Certificate System without requiring a full
CS installation.

HSM Integration:

* Works with any PKCS#11 HSM token

items.fromString:
OCSP responder now returns standard error codes for internal errors::
Before this update, if the Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) responder encountered an internal error, such as missing Certificate Revocation List (CRL) data, it threw an exception. OCSP clients then incorrectly interpreted this exception as an invalid response.
+
With this release, the OCSP responder has been updated to return a proper internal error code as defined in RFC 6960.
+
As a result, clients can now correctly identify when an internal error occurs on the responder side instead of treating the response as invalid.

items.fromString: Fixed invalid Tomcat executable path and Tomcat startup script paths referenced in systemd service files that caused pkispawn failure. The paths were corrected to /usr/sbin instead of /usr/bin, and an invalid inline comment in the service file was removed.
items.toString:
`pkispawn` no longer fails due to invalid Tomcat paths in systemd service files::
Before this update, systemd service files referenced incorrect paths for the Tomcat executable and startup scripts, pointing to `/usr/bin` instead of `/usr/sbin`. Additionally, an invalid inline comment was present in the service configuration. As a consequence, the `pkispawn` utility failed during deployment.
+
With this release, the executable and script paths have been corrected to `/usr/sbin`, and the invalid comment has been removed from the service files.
+
As a result, `pkispawn` now successfully starts the Tomcat service and completes the installation without encountering path-related errors.

items.fromString:
The Certificate System now supports ML-DSA keys and signatures::
You can now install a Certificate System (CS) that uses Module-Lattice-based Digital Signature Algorithm (ML-DSA) for both key types and signatures. Because ML-DSA is standardized by NIST to withstand future quantum computing threats, the CS can now generate and manage quantum-resistant certificates. This release supports ML-DSA at three NIST-defined security levels: ML-DSA-44, 65, and 87.
items.toString:
The Certificate System now supports ML-DSA keys and signatures::
With this enhancement, the Certificate System supports the Module-Lattice-based Digital Signature Algorithm (ML-DSA) for both keys and signatures. Because ML-DSA is standardized by NIST to withstand potential quantum computing threats, the Certificate System can now generate and manage quantum-resistant certificates.
+
This release supports ML-DSA at three NIST-defined security levels: ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, and ML-DSA-87.

items.fromString: As a Product Owner, the need exists to create an RFE that will focus specifically on verifying RHCS installations and automation to ensure ML-DSA keys function correctly, building upon PKI Team’s work on the RHEL RFE, [[RFE] Add support to ML-DSA|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHEL-143038].
items.toString:
Add support for ML-DSA (Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm) post-quantum cryptography to Red Hat Certificate System.

  This includes:

* CA can issue certificates to users with ML-DSA keys
* CA can sign certificates using its own ML-DSA signing key
* OCSP responder can sign responses with ML-DSA
* Certificate validation works correctly with ML-DSA signatures
* Full PKI stack (PKI → TomcatJSS → JSS → NSS) handles ML-DSA operations
properly

  Dependencies:

* ML-DSA support in NSS
* ML-DSA support in JSS

Description of problem:
The command - pki-server subsystem-cert-update - fails with "ERROR: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'replace'" if used with CA subsystem. The warning "WARNING: Certificate request not found" is also seen in the output. For example, see below:

# pki-server subsystem-cert-update -i topology-02-CA ca signing
WARNING: Certificate request not found
ERROR: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'replace'
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/lib/python3.6/site-packages/pki/server/pkiserver.py", line 41, in <module>
    cli.execute(sys.argv)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.6/site-packages/pki/server/cli/__init__.py", line 144, in execute
    super().execute(args)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.6/site-packages/pki/cli/__init__.py", line 217, in execute
    module.execute(module_args)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.6/site-packages/pki/cli/__init__.py", line 217, in execute
    module.execute(module_args)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.6/site-packages/pki/cli/__init__.py", line 217, in execute
    module.execute(module_args)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.6/site-packages/pki/server/cli/subsystem.py", line 1285, in execute
    subsystem.store_system_cert_request(system_cert)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.6/site-packages/pki/server/subsystem.py", line 394, in store_system_cert_request
    csr_pem = pki.nssdb.convert_csr(csr_data, 'base64', 'pem')
  File "/usr/lib/python3.6/site-packages/pki/nssdb.py", line 146, in convert_csr
    footers=[CSR_FOOTER, LEGACY_CSR_FOOTER])
  File "/usr/lib/python3.6/site-packages/pki/nssdb.py", line 102, in convert_data
    data = data.replace('\r', '').replace('\n', '')
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'replace'


The CA signing CSR is on the system:
# ls /etc/pki/topology-02-CA/certs/ca_signing.csr
/etc/pki/topology-02-CA/certs/ca_signing.csr

*On a separate but similar issue, if pki-server subsystem-cert-update is run for any other instance besides the CA, an error about no CA subsystem is returned:

# pki-server subsystem-cert-update -i topology-02-KRA kra transport
ERROR: No CA subsystem in instance topology-02-KRA.


Version-Release number of selected component (if applicable):
# rpm -qa | grep redhat-pki
redhat-pki-console-theme-11.5.0-1.module+el8pki+21377+0ad73d5f.noarch
redhat-pki-javadoc-11.5.0-1.module+el8pki+21377+0ad73d5f.noarch

redhat-pki-ocsp-11.5.0-1.module+el8pki+21377+0ad73d5f.noarch
redhat-pki-base-11.5.0-1.module+el8pki+21377+0ad73d5f.noarch
redhat-pki-tools-11.5.0-1.module+el8pki+21377+0ad73d5f.x86_64
redhat-pki-console-11.5.0-1.module+el8pki+21377+0ad73d5f.noarch
redhat-pki-server-11.5.0-1.module+el8pki+21377+0ad73d5f.noarch
redhat-pki-ca-11.5.0-1.module+el8pki+21377+0ad73d5f.noarch
redhat-pki-kra-11.5.0-1.module+el8pki+21377+0ad73d5f.noarch
redhat-pki-tks-11.5.0-1.module+el8pki+21377+0ad73d5f.noarch
redhat-pki-11.5.0-1.module+el8pki+21377+0ad73d5f.x86_64
python3-redhat-pki-11.5.0-1.module+el8pki+21377+0ad73d5f.noarch
redhat-pki-java-11.5.0-1.module+el8pki+21377+0ad73d5f.noarch
redhat-pki-est-11.5.0-1.module+el8pki+21377+0ad73d5f.noarch
redhat-pki-tps-11.5.0-1.module+el8pki+21377+0ad73d5f.noarch

# cat /etc/redhat-release 
Red Hat Enterprise Linux release 8.8 (Ootpa)

# cat /usr/share/pki/CS_SERVER_VERSION 
Red Hat Certificate System 10.6.0


How reproducible:
Always

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Install redhat-ds 11.7 and redhat-pki 10.6 modules in RHEL 8.8
2. Install directory server, CA and KRA
3. Run the command - pki-server subsystem-cert-update -i <CA instance name> ca signing
4. Run the command - pki-server subsystem-cert-update -i <KRA instance name> kra storage

Actual results:
3. command fails and warning & error is seen:
WARNING: Certificate request not found
ERROR: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'replace'

4. command fails with the error:
ERROR: No CA subsystem in instance topology-02-KRA.

Expected results:
pki-server subsystem-cert-update command should not fail and should work for other instances besides CA

Additional info:
No error in debug log.

Some similarity to the message in https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1340455

Missing instance validation in Java CLI subcommands causes stack trace errors::
Several `pki-server` subcommands fail with a stack trace error instead of a useful error message under the following conditions:

* An instance is not explicitly defined with the "-i" argument
* An instance is not specified at all
* An incorrect, non-existent instance is specified. 

+
As a workaround, explicitly call the instance with the ‘-i’ argument.
+
As a result of setting this property, the utility can correctly locate the instance configuration and execute the command without triggering a stack trace.
items.toString:
Missing instance validation in Java CLI subcommands causes stack trace errors::
Several `pki-server` subcommands throw a stack trace error instead of a user-friendly error message when the specified instance does not exist, or when no instance is specified and the default, such as `pki-tomcat`, does not exist on the system.
+
As a workaround, always specify a valid instance name with the `-i` flag. For example:
+
[subs=+qutoes]
----
# pki-server ca-cert-find -i
----
+
As a result of setting this property, the utility can correctly locate the instance configuration and execute the command without triggering a stack trace.

Missing instance validation in Java CLI subcommands causes stack trace errors::
Before this update, several Java-based `pki-server` subcommands lacked proper validation for the PKI-Tomcat instance path. If a command was executed without an explicitly defined instance, the system defaulted to a non-existent path. This resulted in a Java stack trace error instead of a clear, actionable error message.
+
As a workaround for this known issue, you must manually define the path to your PKI-Tomcat instance by setting the `catalina.base` system property.
+
As a result of setting this property, the utility can correctly locate the instance configuration and execute the command without triggering a stack trace.

The `JAVA_HOME` reference in `tomcat.conf` must be manually updated to Java 17::
When upgrading to Red Hat Certificate System (RHCS) 10.8, the` tomcat.conf` file may still reference the Java 8 JDK path instead of the compatible Java 17 JDK. Because newer RHCS components require Java 17, this configuration mismatch results in an `UnsupportedClassVersionError`, preventing the PKI instance from starting.
+
As a workaround for this issue, you must manually update the `JAVA_HOME` path in the `/etc/pki/<pki_instance>/tomcat.conf` file. Change the value from `/usr/lib/jvm/jre-1.8.0-openjdk` to `/usr/lib/jvm/jre-17-openjdk`.
+
As a result of updating this reference, Tomcat can correctly load the required Java 17 environment, allowing RHCS 10.8 services to start successfully.

Updating `JAVA_HOME` in `tomcat.conf` resolves Tomcat startup failures::
Before this update, upgrading to Red Hat Certificate System (RHCS) 10.8 while retaining Java 8 caused Tomcat to fail because newer components require Java 17. The system would encounter an `UnsupportedClassVersionError`, preventing the PKI instance from starting correctly.
+
As a workaround for this issue, update the `JAVA_HOME` path in `/etc/pki/<pki_instance>/tomcat.conf` from `/usr/lib/jvm/jre-1.8.0-openjdk` to `/usr/lib/jvm/jre-17-openjdk`.
+
As a result, Tomcat starts correctly and the RHCS 10.8 services function as expected with Java 17.

The `JAVA_HOME` reference in `tomcat.conf` must be manually updated to Java 17::
When upgrading to Red Hat Certificate System (RHCS) 10.8, the` tomcat.conf` file may still reference the Java 8 JDK path instead of the compatible Java 17 JDK. Because newer RHCS components require Java 17, this configuration mismatch results in an `UnsupportedClassVersionError`, preventing the PKI instance from starting.
+
As a workaround for this issue, you must manually update the `JAVA_HOME` path in the `/etc/pki/<pki_instance>/tomcat.conf` file. Change the value from `/usr/lib/jvm/jre-1.8.0-openjdk` to `/usr/lib/jvm/jre-17-openjdk`.
+
As a result of updating this reference, Tomcat can correctly load the required Java 17 environment, allowing RHCS 10.8 services to start successfully.

RHCS upgrade from 10.6 to 10.8 no longer results in Java version errors::
Before this update, upgrading Red Hat Certificate System (RHCS) from version 10.6 to 10.8 failed to update the Java configuration in the `tomcat.conf` file. The file incorrectly retained a reference to Java 8, which caused an `UnsupportedClassVersionError` when the system attempted to run components compiled for Java 17.
+
With this release, the upgrade process correctly updates the Java path in `tomcat.conf` to reflect the required version.
+
As a result, the transition to RHCS 10.8 ensures compatibility with Java 17, and the service starts successfully without Java-related errors.

Updating `JAVA_HOME` in `tomcat.conf` resolves Tomcat startup failures::
Before this update, upgrading to Red Hat Certificate System (RHCS) 10.8 while retaining Java 8 caused Tomcat to fail because newer components require Java 17. The system would encounter an `UnsupportedClassVersionError`, preventing the PKI instance from starting correctly.
+
As a workaround for this issue, update the `JAVA_HOME` path in `/etc/pki/<pki_instance>/tomcat.conf` from `/usr/lib/jvm/jre-1.8.0-openjdk` to `/usr/lib/jvm/jre-17-openjdk`.
+
As a result, Tomcat starts correctly and the RHCS 10.8 services function as expected with Java 17.

h3. How reproducible:

Always
h3. Steps to Reproduce:

1. Install older version of RHCS subsystems (i.e. RHCS 10.6 on RHEL 8.8)

# grep JAVA_HOME /etc/pki/topology-02-CA/tomcat.conf
JAVA_HOME="/usr/lib/jvm/jre-1.8.0-openjdk"{code}

{code:java}
# pki-server --debug ca-cert-find -i topology-02-CA{code}

{code:java}
Error: A JNI error has occurred, please check your installation and try again
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.UnsupportedClassVersionError: org/dogtagpki/server/cli/PKIServerCLI has been compiled by a more recent version of the Java Runtime (class file version 61.0), this version of the Java Runtime only recognizes class file versions up to 52.0

        at java.net.URLClassLoader.access$100(URLClassLoader.java:74)
        at java.net.URLClassLoader$1.run(URLClassLoader.java:369)
        at java.net.URLClassLoader$1.run(URLClassLoader.java:363)
        at java.security.AccessController.doPrivileged(Native Method)
        at java.net.URLClassLoader.findClass(URLClassLoader.java:362)

        at java.lang.ClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoader.java:351)
        at sun.launcher.LauncherHelper.checkAndLoadMain(LauncherHelper.java:621){code}
h3. Expected results:

Java 17 JVM path will be updated in tomcat.conf after RHCS upgrade:

JAVA_HOME="/usr/lib/jvm/jre-17-openjdk"

 
h3. Additional info:

Workaround is to manually update the JAVA_HOME path in /etc/pki/<pki_instance>/tomcat.conf from:

{code:java}
JAVA_HOME="/usr/lib/jvm/jre-17-openjdk"
{code}
to:
{code:java}
JAVA_HOME="/usr/lib/jvm/jre-17-openjdk"
{code}

After upgrading from RHCS 10.6 to 10.8, the existing tomcat.conf files contain JAVA_HOME="/usr/lib/jvm/jre-1.8.0-openjdk", resulting in the below error:
{code:java}
Error: A JNI error has occurred, please check your installation and try again
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.UnsupportedClassVersionError: org/dogtagpki/server/cli/PKIServerCLI has been compiled by a more recent version of the Java Runtime (class file version 61.0), this version of the Java Runtime only recognizes class file versions up to 52.0{code}
h3. Version-Release number of selected component (if applicable):
{code:java}
# rpm -qa | grep -e ^redhat-pki-11 -e openjdk
java-17-openjdk-17.0.16.0.8-2.el8.x86_64
java-17-openjdk-headless-17.0.16.0.8-2.el8.x86_64
redhat-pki-11.6.1-2.module+el8pki+22942+ec484924.x86_64
java-1.8.0-openjdk-headless-1.8.0.462.b08-2.el8.x86_64
java-1.8.0-openjdk-1.8.0.462.b08-2.el8.x86_64
java-1.8.0-openjdk-devel-1.8.0.462.b08-2.el8.x86_64
java-17-openjdk-devel-17.0.16.0.8-2.el8.x86_64{code}
{code:java}
# cat /etc/redhat-release 
Red Hat Enterprise Linux release 8.10 (Ootpa){code}
{code:java}
# dnf module info redhat-pki
Name             : redhat-pki
Stream           : 10 [d][e][a]
Version          : 8100020250319103323
Context          : f9354743
Architecture     : x86_64
Profiles         : common [d]
Default profiles : common
Repo             : certsys-10.8-for-rhel-8-x86_64-rpms
Summary          : Red Hat Certificate System 10.8
Description      : A module for Red Hat Certificate System packages.
Requires         : pki-deps:[10.6]
                 : platform:[el8]{code}
h3. How reproducible:

Always
h3. Steps to Reproduce:

1. Install older version of RHCS subsystems (i.e. RHCS 10.6 on RHEL 8.8)
2. Follow upgrade procedure to RHCS 10.8 on RHEL 8.10
3. Look at tomcat.conf file for the CA, for example:
{code:java}
# grep JAVA_HOME /etc/pki/topology-02-CA/tomcat.conf
JAVA_HOME="/usr/lib/jvm/jre-1.8.0-openjdk"{code}
4. Use a command that creates a separate JVM
{code:java}
# pki-server --debug ca-cert-find -i topology-02-CA{code}
h3. Actual results:

The JAVA_HOME variable is using java 8 instead of java 17, resulting in the below error:
{code:java}
Error: A JNI error has occurred, please check your installation and try again
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.UnsupportedClassVersionError: org/dogtagpki/server/cli/PKIServerCLI has been compiled by a more recent version of the Java Runtime (class file version 61.0), this version of the Java Runtime only recognizes class file versions up to 52.0
        at java.lang.ClassLoader.defineClass1(Native Method)
        at java.lang.ClassLoader.defineClass(ClassLoader.java:756)
        at java.security.SecureClassLoader.defineClass(SecureClassLoader.java:142)
        at java.net.URLClassLoader.defineClass(URLClassLoader.java:473)
        at java.net.URLClassLoader.access$100(URLClassLoader.java:74)
        at java.net.URLClassLoader$1.run(URLClassLoader.java:369)
        at java.net.URLClassLoader$1.run(URLClassLoader.java:363)
        at java.security.AccessController.doPrivileged(Native Method)
        at java.net.URLClassLoader.findClass(URLClassLoader.java:362)
        at java.lang.ClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoader.java:418)
        at sun.misc.Launcher$AppClassLoader.loadClass(Launcher.java:352)
        at java.lang.ClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoader.java:351)
        at sun.launcher.LauncherHelper.checkAndLoadMain(LauncherHelper.java:621){code}
h3. Expected results:

Java 17 JVM path will be updated in tomcat.conf after RHCS upgrade:

JAVA_HOME="/usr/lib/jvm/jre-17-openjdk"

 
h3. Additional info:

Workaround is to manually update the JAVA_HOME path in /etc/pki/<pki_instance>/tomcat.conf from:
JAVA_HOME="/usr/lib/jvm/jre-17-openjdk"
to:
JAVA_HOME="/usr/lib/jvm/jre-17-openjdk"

RHCS upgrade from 10.6 to 10.8 no longer results in Java version errors::
Before this update, upgrading Red Hat Certificate System (RHCS) from version 10.6 to 10.8 failed to update the Java configuration in the `tomcat.conf` file. The file incorrectly retained a reference to Java 8, which caused an `UnsupportedClassVersionError` when the system attempted to run components compiled for Java 17.
+
With this release, the upgrade process correctly updates the Java path in `tomcat.conf` to reflect the required version.
+
As a result, the transition to RHCS 10.8 ensures compatibility with Java 17, and the service starts successfully without Java-related errors.

*Description of problem:*
The error message should be optimized for commands with input file option when used with a nonexistent file. 

For example:
pki 'ca-profile-add asdf' or 'ca-profile-mod asdf' command

pki -d /opt/pki/certdb -h pki1.example.com -p 21443  -u kradmin -W <nonexistent_password_file>

pki tps-profile-add --input asdfasdf

*Version-Release number of selected component (if applicable):*
redhat-pki-10.11.1-3.module+el8pki+12951+5b86c4f5.src.rpm

*How reproducible:*
Always

*Steps to Reproduce:
*
1. Execute the below command:
